sub_problem: Can reversibility-triggered close-encounter microsteps and offline calibration improve trust without drifting into a TRACE or JANUS clone?
note: Direct recovery after two timed-out automated probe attempts.
associations: Treat round-trip error as an online trust signal rather than an offline diagnostic only.
Use geometric encounter triage to decide when the expensive reversible path should activate.
Calibrate named presets offline so the runtime policy stays tiny and deterministic.

forced_bridges.mechanism: Use angular sweep intervals as a broad-phase encounter queue instead of scanning all pairs.
Use forward-backward mismatch as the trigger for shrinking dt or enabling encounter microsteps.
Fit softening and encounter thresholds offline so the online kernel can stay simple.

anomaly_results.result: The reversible micro-step wrapper still survives if activation is local, symmetric, and driven by a deterministic encounter queue.

anomaly_results.constraint: Cross-runtime replay must stay within tolerance without bitwise integer arithmetic.
anomaly_results.result: NaN behavior, trigger thresholds, and output sampling become first-class design parameters; JANUS-style exact reversibility is out of scope.
Offline-calibrated presets plus visible round-trip diagnostics are more defensible than a large menu of hidden accuracy knobs.

steering_directions.rationale: It is the smallest branch that is still genuinely novel and directly addresses the falsifier's strongest attack.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement angular sweep encounter triage, reversible microsteps, and a forward/reverse trust report on the same scenarios.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Flyby energy spikes fall while round-trip error becomes predictive of failure cases.

steering_directions.direction: Hold a resolution-aware honesty layer in reserve.
steering_directions.rationale: Invariant projection and resolution-coupled softening may be useful, but they should only be promoted if they improve trust without masking bad physics.
steering_directions.first_step: Measure whether projection corrections stay small and whether scale-aware softening reduces alias-like artifacts without erasing orbital structure.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Drift and visual artifacts improve together; otherwise retire the branch.

steering_directions.direction: Retire large-N performance ideas from the main thesis.
steering_directions.rationale: Neighbor trees, event-sparse far fields, and patch streaming are interesting but threaten to turn the project into a performance paper instead of an audited reference kernel.
steering_directions.first_step: Keep the direct-sum kernel as the reference path and do not let performance branches define the headline contribution.
steering_directions.expected_signal: The novelty story stays narrow and easier to verify against REBOUND and educational baselines.

validation_checks: Compare close-flyby energy drift against a uniform small-dt baseline and REBOUND IAS15.
Measure whether round-trip error rises before visible orbital failure across all test scenes.
Check that calibrated presets remain ordered on held-out scenarios instead of overfitting one case.
Reject any branch whose only measurable benefit is speed on small N without a trust gain.
